title: Flower colour in a meadow population
body: A class surveys a large, randomly mating meadow population of a wild plant in which flower colour is controlled by one gene with two alleles. The allele R for red flowers is completely dominant over the allele r for white flowers. Out of 1000 plants counted, 910 have red flowers and 90 have white flowers. The students note that there has been no migration of plants into or out of the meadow, no new mutation has been recorded, and neither colour seems to give any advantage in survival or seed production. They decide to treat the population as being in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium and use the equation p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1, where p is the frequency of R and q is the frequency of r, to estimate genotype numbers.
